purpose: Decision Framework: the clear list of questions, the information already held (verified), and the information missing before any decision can be made. Official links are context/verification targets.

questions.question: Should any strategy be promoted to the live leaderboard with rewards?
questions.have: 8 registered research designs (singles, parlays, player-prop combos); validation gates G1-G8 all BLOCKED except G1; 0 eligible strategies; no verified operator prices or out-of-sample skill evidence.
questions.missing: Verified timestamped operator prices, chronological out-of-sample evidence, aligned joint outcomes for combos, and an immutable prospective forecast ledger.
questions.impact: No rewards can be awarded. All strategies remain BLOCKED until the missing evidence exists.

questions.question: Which sources can be trusted for live updates?
questions.have: nfl.com standings / Week 10 schedule / Week 9 scores / Week 10 injury report verified on 2026-11-14 (202 arithmetic and cross-capture checks PASS); NGS Week 9 passing verified; NIST statistical references checked.
questions.missing: An official real-time feed or API; retained raw HTTP capture. Dynamic official pages can change after retrieval.
questions.impact: Snapshots remain point-in-time extracts; freshness must be re-verified each cycle, and older snapshots are archived rather than deleted.

questions.question: Can we originate our own NFL lines without market inputs?
questions.have: B0 benchmark method (derived from verified scoring rates); 14 Week 10 benchmark lines generated; zero venue adjustment by design.
questions.missing: Calibration against official lines; venue, roster, opponent-strength, pace and uncertainty adjustments; a frozen threshold set.
questions.impact: Originated lines remain illustrative derived benchmarks, not official lines, fair prices or recommendations.

questions.question: How do we establish skill and remove luck from strategy evaluation?
questions.have: No out-of-sample skill evidence exists; luck cannot be eliminated by any finite test; proposed proper scoring (Brier / log loss) against fixed baselines.
questions.missing: Prospective immutable ledger, pre-registered trials, family-wise adjusted evidence, and an untouched final test period.
questions.impact: No skill designation is made. Abstaining is the correct result when evidence is missing.

questions.question: What correlation values are needed to price parlays and player-prop combos?
questions.have: 3 descriptive team-level correlations (net points/game vs win fraction, rank correlation, points-for/game vs win fraction); all bet-leg dependence cells blank.
questions.missing: Aligned event-level paired outcomes, market thresholds, and joint-distribution evidence for multi-leg combinations.
questions.impact: Combinations cannot be priced. Unknown dependence is never treated as independence.

questions.question: How should injuries and backup-replacement deficiencies (2nd/3rd/4th string on offense and defense) be incorporated?
questions.have: Week 10 injury report bounded sample (149 rows across 6 games); 10 official news headlines (QB situations, IR placements); NGS Week 9 passing data (30 QBs).
questions.missing: Depth-chart/backup tracking from official sources, final inactive lists, and official gamebook starter data.
questions.impact: Availability-dependent strategies remain blocked; practice participation is not game clearance.

questions.question: What reward structure should the leaderboard competition use?
questions.have: Proposed paper-points rule: reward 100 x the positive family-adjusted lower bound of paired mean Brier improvement over a pre-registered baseline, only after all gates PASS.
questions.missing: Any strategy passing all applicable gates; no cash rewards, bankroll allocation or wagering.
questions.impact: No rewards are awarded. The rule is project design only, not an official sporting rule.

questions.question: What is the release and deployment policy?
questions.have: Site live on GitHub Pages; offline link checks PASS; review flags are non-blocking; snapshot archived per refresh.
questions.missing: None critical. Each release must re-verify the combined data and confirm no broken links before deploy.
questions.impact: Publish the research and all gaps; never publish actionable selections or reward a blocked strategy.

questions.question: Which strategy families (single bet, parlay, player prop) should be prioritized?
questions.have: 8 registered designs spanning singles (spread baseline, total/pace, moneyline calibration), parlays (cross-game joint value) and player props (QB efficiency, receiver opportunity, RB workload, same-game combos).
questions.missing: Evidence to rank them; no validated edge in any family; no bet-leg dependence dataset.
questions.impact: All families remain equally blocked until evidence appears; prioritization is a research question, not a promotion decision.

questions.question: How do we verify every table row against an official source?
questions.have: Every published data row carries an official source link; offline link checker; arithmetic and cross-capture checks (202 checks PASS on the 2026-11-14 refresh); unverified values left blank and flagged.
questions.missing: External HTTP liveness is not asserted by the offline checker; source links are verification targets, not proof of cell-level accuracy.
questions.impact: Unverified values stay blank and flagged for review; no value is inferred or filled in.
